Rashi on Pesachim 91b:11:1.english: Optional, and overrides Shabbat - [This is said] in astonishment.

Rashi on Pesachim 91b:12:1.hebrew: ידקדקו בו - משום שאינן בני תורה, יחמירו עליו לדקדק ויפסילוהו על חנם:
Rashi on Pesachim 91b:12:1.english: They will be meticulous with it - Because they are not Torah scholars, they will be stringent regarding it to be [overly] meticulous, and they will disqualify it needlessly.

Rashi on Pesachim 91b:13:1.english: This is how we read [the text]: The Sages taught: "Paschal lamb, matzah, and bitter herbs, on the first [is] mandatory, etc." - "On the first" [means] the first night.

Rashi on Pesachim 91b:14:1.hebrew: אהייא קאי - מכאן ואילך רשות דתנא קמא. אי נימא אפסח, פסח כל שבעה מי איכא:
Rashi on Pesachim 91b:14:1.english: To which does it refer - [To] "from here on it is optional" of the Tanna Kamma. If we say [it refers] to the Paschal lamb, is there a Paschal lamb all seven [days]?

Rashi on Pesachim 91b:14:2.hebrew: ואלא אמצה ומרור - ועלה מהדר ר"ש: אף בראשון דקאמרת חובה, באנשים הוא דהויא, אבל בנשים רשות:
Rashi on Pesachim 91b:14:2.english: Rather, [it refers] to matza and bitter herbs - And upon that [clause], Rabbi Shimon responds: Even on the first [night], which you said [is] obligatory, it is [obligatory] for men, whereas for women [it is] optional.

Rashi on Pesachim 91b:15:1.hebrew: לית ליה לר"ש - והא ליכא למימר דליהדר אמרור לחודיה, דסתמא מצה ומרור בהדי הדדי כתיב "על מצות ומרורים", וכשם שנשים באכילת מצה חובה, הכי נמי במרור:
Rashi on Pesachim 91b:15:1.english: Does Rabbi Shimon not [accept] - And one cannot say that he was referring to maror alone, for ordinarily matza and maror are written together: "with matzot and bitter herbs," and just as women are obligated in eating matza, so too [are they obligated] in maror.

Rashi on Pesachim 91b:15:2.hebrew: הואיל וישנן בבל תאכל חמץ - דהשוה הכתוב אשה לאיש לכל עונשין שבתורה, דכתיב (במדבר ה׳:ו׳) ״איש או אשה כי יעשו מכל חטאת האדם״ וגו':
Rashi on Pesachim 91b:15:2.english: Since they are subject to [the prohibition of] “You shall not eat leavened bread” - For Scripture equated a woman to a man with respect to all punishments in the Torah, as it is written (Numbers 5:6): “When a man or woman commits any sin of man,” etc.

Rashi on Pesachim 91b:16:1.hebrew: אלא - הכי קאמר: פסח, מצה ומרור בראשון — חובה, מכאן ואילך — רשות; וקאי האי "מכאן ואילך" אמצה ומרור. ור"ש פליג אפסח דקאמרת בראשון חובה: באנשים הוא דהוה חובה, אבל בנשים — רשות; ורבי שמעון לטעמיה:
Rashi on Pesachim 91b:16:1.english: Rather - This is what it is saying: The Paschal lamb, matzah, and bitter herbs on the first [day are] mandatory; from here on, [it is] optional. And this [phrase], "from here on," refers to matzah and bitter herbs. And Rabbi Shimon disagrees regarding [the] Paschal lamb, [of] which you said [that] on the first [day it is] mandatory: [it is] for men that it is mandatory, whereas for women [it is] optional; and Rabbi Shimon [follows] his own reasoning.

Rashi on Pesachim 91b:17:1.hebrew: אונן טובל ואוכל את פסחו לערב - ואף על פי שעדיין לא נקבר, דאין אנינות מן התורה אלא ביום, שנאמר (ויקרא י׳:י״ט): הן היום הקריבו — ואני אונן — ואכלתי חטאת היום; יום אסור, לילה מותר. וטבילה בעי, וזו אחת מאחת עשרה מעלות דחומר בקודש (חגיגה דף כא.): האונן והמחוסר כפורים צריכין טבילה לקודש. מתוך שנאסרו עד עכשיו בקדשים, אצרכינהו רבנן טבילה, ואף על פי שמחוסר כפורים טבל אתמול. אבל לא יאכל אונן לערב בשאר קדשים, דאסור אנינות לילה מדרבנן, ולגבי פסח לא העמידו דבריהן במקום כרת:
Rashi on Pesachim 91b:17:1.english: An acute mourner immerses and eats his Paschal lamb in the evening - Even though [the deceased] has not yet been buried, because acute mourning by Torah law applies only during the day, as it is stated (Leviticus 10:19): "Behold, today they offered" — while I am an acute mourner — "and had I eaten a sin-offering today"; [during the] day it is prohibited, [at] night it is permitted. And he requires immersion, and this is one of the eleven stringencies of sacrificial food (Chagigah 21a): "An acute mourner and one lacking atonement require immersion for sacrificial food." Because they were prohibited until now from [eating] sacrificial food, the Rabbis required them [to undergo] immersion, even though one lacking atonement [already] immersed yesterday. However, an acute mourner may not eat of other sacrificial food in the evening, because acute mourning at night is prohibited by rabbinic decree; whereas regarding the Paschal lamb, [the Rabbis] did not uphold their words in the face of excision [karet].

Rashi on Pesachim 91b:17:2.english: One who hears about his dead [relative] - [On] the day of hearing [the news], he is an acute mourner by rabbinic law.

Rashi on Pesachim 91b:1:1.english: Slaves and minors, because of promiscuity - of homosexual intercourse.

Rashi on Pesachim 91b:2:1.hebrew: אין שוחטין עליה כל עיקר - ואפי' טפילה, דלא שייכא ביה מידי, ואי אכלה ביה הוה פסח נאכל שלא למנויו. וה"ה לעבדים דאין אוכלין בו. וכי אכלי עבדים ונשים בראשון, שהן רשות בו, אבל בשני לא, דאפי' מרשות אימעוט, כדלקמן:
Rashi on Pesachim 91b:2:1.english: We do not slaughter on her behalf at all - Even [as] an ancillary [participant], for she has no connection to it whatsoever, and if she were to eat of it, the Paschal [offering] would be eaten by one not registered for it. And the same applies to slaves, that they may not eat of it. And when slaves and women eat [of it] on the first [Pesaḥ], [it is because] they are optional with regard to it; but on the second [Pesaḥ] not, for they were excluded even from [being] optional, as [explained] below.

Rashi on Pesachim 91b:3:1.hebrew: במכסת נפשות - מדלא כתב אנשים, אפי' אשה במשמע:
Rashi on Pesachim 91b:3:1.english: According to the number of the souls - Since [Scripture] did not write "men," even a woman is implied.

Rashi on Pesachim 91b:3:2.hebrew: כתיב בשני חטאו ישא האיש ההוא - והכי משמע ליה קרא: ״והאיש אשר הוא טהור ובדרך לא היה וחדל לעשות הפסח״ — ראשון, ונכרת; ״כי קרבן ה'״ כו' — ״כי״ לשון שימוש ״אי״, כשקרבן ה' לא הקריב במועדו — בשני — ״חטאו ישא״. והכי דריש בפרק מי שהיה טמא (לקמן פסחים צג.) אליבא דר"י. א"נ: ״קרבן ה' לא הקריב במועדו״ — בשני — ״חטאו ישא״:
Rashi on Pesachim 91b:3:2.english: It is written regarding the second [Pesach]: "That man shall bear his sin" - And thus does the verse imply to him: "And the man who is pure, and was not on a journey, and refrained from making the Pesach [offering]" — [referring to] the first [Pesach], and he is cut off [from his people]; "Because the offering of the Lord, etc." — [the word] ki ["because"] is used in the sense of iy ["if"], [meaning] when he did not offer the offering of the Lord in its appointed time — [that is,] on the second [Pesach] — "he shall bear his sin." And thus it is expounded in the chapter Mi Shehayah Tamei (below, Pesachim 93a) according to Rabbi Yehuda. Alternatively: "The offering of the Lord he did not offer in its appointed time" — [that is,] on the second [Pesach] — "he shall bear his sin."

Rashi on Pesachim 91b:5:1.hebrew: וכתיב בשני ונכרתה הנפש ההיא - דאע"ג דאראשון קאי, מיהו כי קרבן ה' אשני קאי, וכדמפרשינן וגמרינן בה כרת לקמן (שם) — האי חטאו ישא מונשא חטאו דמברך את השם, דכתיב ביה את ה' הוא מגדף ונכרת וגו', והוי כמאן דכתיב נפש בגופיה:
Rashi on Pesachim 91b:5:1.english: And it is written regarding the second [Pesach], “that soul shall be cut off” - For even though [that clause] refers to the first [Pesach], nevertheless “for the offering of the Lord [he did not bring in its appointed time]” refers to the second [Pesach], and as we explain and derive karet for it later on (there) — [deriving] this [phrase] “he shall bear his sin” from “he shall bear his sin” of the one who blasphemes the Name, concerning whom it is written: “he blasphemes the Lord, and [that soul] shall be cut off, etc.” — and [thus] it is as though “soul” were written in [the passage of the second Pesach] itself.

Rashi on Pesachim 91b:5:2.hebrew: ואלא האיש - דגבי פסח, מאי עביד ליה? ליכתוב "חטאו ישא" ותו לא:
Rashi on Pesachim 91b:5:2.english: But "the man" - [which is written] regarding [the second] Pesach, what does [Rabbi Yosei] do with it? Let [Scripture] write "he shall bear his sin," and nothing more.

Rashi on Pesachim 91b:6:1.english: It is written concerning the first [Pesach], “man” - Later [the Gemara] asks: What “man” is written concerning the first [Pesach]?

Rashi on Pesachim 91b:8:1.hebrew: איש זוכה - לאחרים בלקיחתו, אם לקח מקח לצורך אחרים או קיבל מתנה לשם אחרים, כדכתיב: "ויקחו איש שה לבית אבות". ואין קטן זוכה, דאין נעשה שליח:
Rashi on Pesachim 91b:8:1.english: A man can acquire - [He acquires] for others through his taking [possession]: if he purchased merchandise for the needs of others or received a gift on behalf of others, as it is written: "They shall take, each man, a lamb for a fathers' house" [Exodus 12:3]. And a minor cannot acquire [for others], because he cannot become an agent.

Rashi on Pesachim 91b:9:1.english: Rather, [from] “according to every man’s eating” - He expounds it to exclude a woman.

Rashi on Pesachim 91b:9:2.hebrew: והא מדר' יוסי סבר לה כר"ש - דאין שוחטין פסח בבמת יחיד, מולא תוכל לזבוח:
Rashi on Pesachim 91b:9:2.english: And since Rabbi Yosei holds like Rabbi Shimon - that we do not slaughter a Paschal lamb on a private altar, [derived] from [the verse], "You may not slaughter."

Rashi on Pesachim 91b:9:3.hebrew: ר"ש נמי סבר לה כר' יוסי - דיליף מאיש לפי אכלו ששוחט פסח על היחיד. דאי לא ס"ל כוותיה, ממאי דהאי באחד לדרשא דידיה אתא? הא טפי משמע שפיר כר"י דאין שוחטין על היחיד:
Rashi on Pesachim 91b:9:3.english: R' Shimon also holds in accordance with R' Yosei - Who derives from "according to every man's eating" that one slaughters a Paschal lamb for an individual. For if [R' Shimon] did not hold like him, from where [would we know] that this [phrase] "in one [of your gates]" comes for his exposition [regarding a private altar]? Behold, it more readily implies well in accordance with R' Yehuda, that one does not slaughter [the Paschal lamb] for an individual.

Rashi on Pesachim 91b:9:4.hebrew: לפי אכלו - בלאו איש נמי נפקא לן מלשון יחיד דשוחטין פסח על היחיד, ואיש דרשינן ליה למעוטי אשה:
Rashi on Pesachim 91b:9:4.english: According to his eating - Even without [the word] "man," we also derive from the singular form that we slaughter a Paschal lamb for an individual, and "man" we expound to exclude a woman.

Tosafot on Pesachim 91b:12:1.hebrew: שמא ידקדקו בו ויביאוהו לידי פסול - תימה, דבעי למימר דגרים מדקדקים ביותר, ודמי להא דאמרינן (חולין דף ד.): "כל מצוה שהחזיקו בה גרים וכותים, הרבה מדקדקים בה יותר מישראל". ובירושל' גריס: "אמר רבי יעקב בר יצחק בשם רבי יוסי: אין עושין חבורות של גרים, שמתוך שהן מקולקלים אין מדקדקין ויביאוהו לידי פסול". ובכל דוכתא נמי חזינן דגרים לא דייקי במצות כישראלים, והכא קאמר דגרים מדקדקים יותר:
Tosafot on Pesachim 91b:12:1.english: "Perhaps they will be meticulous with it and cause it to become disqualified" - This is astonishing, for [the Gemara] means to say that converts are exceedingly meticulous, and it is similar to that which we say (Chullin 4a): "Any mitzvah that converts and Cutheans have taken hold of, they are much more meticulous about it than [born] Jews." Yet in the Jerusalem Talmud it reads: "Rabbi Yaakov bar Yitzchak said in the name of Rabbi Yose: We do not form groups of converts, for since they are lax [in observance], they are not meticulous and will cause it to become disqualified." And everywhere else as well we see that converts are not as exact in [performing] the mitzvot as [born] Jews, yet here it says that converts are more meticulous.

Tosafot on Pesachim 91b:5:1.hebrew: וכתיב בשני "ונכרתה הנפש ההיא" אפי' אשה - ולא נפקא לרבי יוסי אשה מ"ככל חקת הפסח", דמהתם מפיק ר"י טפילה; דאי לאו "הנפש ההיא", "ככל חקת הפסח" לא הוה מוקמינן אלא לטפילה כר' יהודה, ו"איש" למעוטי חובה. הלכך גלי "הנפש ההיא" דלא ממעטינן אשה מ"איש":
Tosafot on Pesachim 91b:5:1.english: "And it is written regarding the second [Pesaḥ], 'that soul shall be cut off,' [meaning] even a woman" - And for Rabbi Yosei, a woman is not derived from "according to the entire statute of the Paschal lamb," because from there Rabbi Yosei derives ancillary participation — for were it not for "that soul," we would only establish "according to the entire statute of the Paschal lamb" for ancillary participation, like Rabbi Yehudah, and "man" [would serve] to exclude [her from] obligation. Therefore, "that soul" reveals that we do not exclude a woman from "man."

Tosafot on Pesachim 91b:5:2.hebrew: איש ולא קטן - תימה, אמאי איצטריך? דהיכן מצינו שחייב קטן במצות? וי"ל דאיצטריך לקטן שהגדיל בין שני פסחים, דס"ד דחייב לעשות פסח שני, קמ"ל דשני תשלומין דראשון הוא. ובפרק מי שהיה טמא (לקמן פסחים דף צג.) משמע דנפקא לן מקרא אחרינא. ובפ' ד' מיתות (סנהדרין דף נד:) נמי קשה, אמאי איצטריך איש פרט לקטן בבא על אשת איש ועל אשת אביו ועל הזכר ועל הבהמה:
Tosafot on Pesachim 91b:5:2.english: "A man" — and not a minor - This is astonishing: why is [a verse] needed [to exclude him]? For where do we find that a minor is obligated in commandments? And one can answer that it is needed for a minor who came of age between the two Pesach [offerings]; for it might have entered your mind that he is obligated to offer the second Pesach, [so the verse] teaches us that the second is a compensation for the first. And in the chapter [entitled] Mi Shehayah Tamei (below, Pesachim 93a), it implies that we derive this from a different verse. And in the chapter [entitled] Arba Mitot (Sanhedrin 54b), it is also difficult: why is "a man" needed [to teach] "excluding a minor" regarding one who has relations with a married woman, or with his father's wife, or with a male, or with an animal?

Tosafot on Pesachim 91b:8:1.hebrew: אי נימא מאיש שה הא מיבעי ליה לכדר' יצחק כו' - תימה לר"י, דבריש פ"ב דקדושין (דף מב.) משמע דמילתיה דרבי יצחק מאיש לפי אכלו נפקא. ואומר ר"י, דהתם משום דמאיש שה מפיק לשליחות, דלא מצי מפיק שליחות מאיש לפי אכלו; לכך נפקא דרבי יצחק מאיש לפי אכלו. אבל תלמודא דהכא נפקא ליה שליחות מדרבי יהושע בן קרחה, ולכך מוקי איש שה לכדרבי יצחק, דמשמע דמיירי בזכיה טפי מאיש לפי אכלו:
Tosafot on Pesachim 91b:8:1.english: If we say [it is derived] from "[every] man a lamb," he needs that for [the derivation of] Rabbi Yitzchak, etc. - The Ri [Rabbeinu Yitzchak] wonders [at this], for at the beginning of the second chapter of Kiddushin (42a) it is implied that Rabbi Yitzchak's statement is derived from "[every] man according to his eating" [Exodus 12:4]. And the Ri says that there [in Kiddushin], it is because [the Gemara] derives agency from "[every] man a lamb," since it cannot derive agency from "[every] man according to his eating"; therefore, [the statement of] Rabbi Yitzchak is derived from "[every] man according to his eating." However, the Talmud here derives agency from [the teaching of] Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korchah, and therefore it establishes "[every] man a lamb" for [the teaching of] Rabbi Yitzchak, since it implies that it is speaking of acquisition more than "[every] man according to his eating."

Tosafot on Pesachim 91b:8:2.hebrew: איש זוכה ואין קטן זוכה - תימה, אמאי איצטריך קרא? והא קי"ל דאין שליחות לקטן, ובפ' קמא דבבא מציעא (דף יב.) מוכח דזכיה מטעם שליחות! וכי תימא מהכא קיי"ל דאין לו שליחות, אכתי קשה אמאי איצטריך למעט דאינו זוכה; הא אפילו לעצמו אין לו זכיה במציאתו אלא מפני דרכי שלום, כדאמרינן בהניזקין (גיטין דף נט.)! ויש לומר דדוקא מציאה, אבל מתנה דדעת אחרת מקנה אותו עדיף, כדמסיק בשנים אוחזין (ב"מ דף יב:); וכן בפרק התקבל (גיטין דף סד:) קאמרינן: צרור וזורקו אגוז ונוטלו — זוכה לעצמו אפי' לגבי קנין דאורייתא:
Tosafot on Pesachim 91b:8:2.english: A man can acquire, and a minor cannot acquire - [This is] astonishing: why is a verse needed? For we hold as an established rule that a minor has no agency, and in the first chapter of Bava Metzia (12a) it is proven that acquisition [on behalf of another] operates on the principle of agency! And if you will say [that] it is from here [that] we establish that he has no agency, it is still difficult why it was necessary to exclude [him from] acquiring [for others]; behold, even for himself he has no acquisition of his found item except on account of the ways of peace, as we say in [the chapter] HaNizakin (Gittin 59a)! And one can say that [that applies] specifically [to] a found item, whereas a gift, where another person's mind transfers ownership to him, is stronger, as [the Gemara] concludes in [the chapter] Shenayim Ochazin (Bava Metzia 12b); and similarly in the chapter Hitkabel (Gittin 64b) we say: [If a minor is given] a pebble and he throws it away, [but] a nut and he takes it — he acquires for himself even with respect to a biblical acquisition.

Tosafot on Pesachim 91b:9:1.hebrew: רבי שמעון נמי סבר לה כרבי יוסי - תימה: דילמא סבר לה כרבי יהודה, ותרתי שמעת מינה, כדאמרינן לעיל לרבי יהודה:
Tosafot on Pesachim 91b:9:1.english: Rabbi Shimon also holds like Rabbi Yosei - This is surprising: perhaps he holds like Rabbi Yehuda, and you learn two [laws] from it, as we said above according to Rabbi Yehuda.
